text:
sophie: quick RFC follow-up: proposing we split tenant-ingress into two surfaces: 1) hotpath runtime (generation, kv cache local), 2) control/batching plane (scheduling, per-tenant limits). Goal: reduce runtime churn and give us flexible QoS. link: https://rfc/internal/tenant-ingress-split :eyes:

rana: high level sounds good. main worry is consistency between runtime cache and batcher decisions. if batcher doesn't see prefix hints we might lose prefix cache hits.

kevin: agreed. three options: A) keep KV only local and batcher asks runtime for hints (RPC on accept), B) lightweight cache-proxy that mirrors prefixes (eventual), C) move small read-only prefix index into control plane.

sophie: perf considerations: A adds sync RPC on accept path; B adds replication complexity; C centralizes index but hurts isolation. Need numbers.

rana: we ran a small sim: option A increased median accept latency by ~0.6ms, p99 by ~2.2ms under load. option B with prefetch hints kept p99 delta under 1ms. logs in the protos channel.

kevin: ops note: sidecar vs colocated pool trade: sidecar = per-worker memory + process mgmt; colocated pool = shared process per host and a local fast socket. Sidecar simplifies ownership but doubles container count.

sophie: rollout idea: start by extracting scheduling decisions to a colocated pool on staging for low-SLO tenants (embeddings), test billing delta, then enable per-tenant soft-limits. If stable, can pursue sidecar for strict low-latency tenants.

kevin: metric contract: batcher must emit per-tenant tokens_emitted, tokens_batched, and backpressure_events. billing-bot: please confirm required schema.

billing-bot: billing schema expected: ["tenant_id","window","tokens_emitted","tokens_billed"] — will subscribe to tokens_batched once we have stable naming.

rana: fairness question: when spikes happen, scheduler either enforces strict leak-bucket or uses weighted sharing. strict leak-bucket protects SLOs but may starve bursty but paid tenants. weighted sharing is fairer but complex. Trade: strict + emergency override for enterprise tenants.

sophie: decision items to close RFC: 1) initial cache model (we lean to lightweight cache-proxy with prefetch hints), 2) initial deployment (colocated pool for embeddings first), 3) accounting model (local counters exported + periodic reconciliation), 4) fairness policy (leak-bucket with override).

kevin: operational checklist: a) CI node-image run at 2x processes, b) healthchecks (ruche probe) for transient CPU bursts, c) socket binding tests across GCP/AWS, d) audit for mTLS if remote.

sophie: I'll update RFC with sequence and add a perf gating appendix. Rana, can you attach the sim logs and the prefetch prototype?

rana: will attach today. small note: prefetch API we used was POST /hint {prefix, ttl}. kept traffic under 0.5req/s per runtime on average.

ops-bot: experiment window set: wed-thu 02:00-06:00 UTC.

kevin: thanks all. reconvene next Tue 10:00 PT to pick start tenants. short sync on slack before that if we hit blockers. :thumbsup:

sophie: booked. thanks!
